findings.detail: The question repeats the structure and answer of M2-S29-T1: two workflows, a fixed prompt chain for the predictable one and dynamic decomposition for the investigation. Wrong option C reuses an earlier wrong option almost word for word. It runs the investigation as a fixed chain with every step defined in advance so each case follows 'the same predictable order', as in M2-S29-T1 option A. It is also close to the M1-S21-T1 wrong option about the same order for every dispute. Correct option E also closely matches the M1-S21-T1 correct answer, which uses the same scenario and the same tools.

blind_answer.reason: The ticket audit checks the same four aspects every time, so a fixed prompt chain with one focused pass per aspect fits it (1.6-S1, K2). The account investigation is open-ended and each tool result can point somewhere new, so dynamic decomposition that generates subtasks from what get_customer or lookup_order reveal fits it (1.6-K3).
